display.title: The Baal Shem Tov's Letter, Delivered Sixteen Years Late
display.summary_short: A rich merchant who never says 'Baruch Hashem' forgets to deliver a letter from the Baal Shem Tov. Sixteen years later, poor and humbled, he finds it, and it turns out to be about him.
display.summary_long: For the Shabbos of Yud-Tes Kislev, the Rosh Hashanah of Chassidus, the storyteller explains why a 'head' of the year gives strength for everything that follows, and how Chassidus began with the Baal Shem Tov. Then the story: Avigdor, a wealthy merchant from Brody, brings the Baal Shem Tov a large donation but credits his success only to his own cleverness and never says 'Baruch Hashem'. The Baal Shem Tov explains from Tehillim that Hashem treasures a Jew's thanks more than the songs of the angels, then asks Avigdor to deliver a sealed letter to a man in Brody. Avigdor forgets it in his suit pocket. Years later his business collapses, and as he prepares to sell the suit he finds the letter, sixteen years late. The man named on it, a poor tailor who always said 'Baruch Hashem' and grew rich, has just been appointed head of the community that very morning. The letter asks him to help its bearer, and gives two signs that come true on the spot.
display.lesson: Everything we have comes from Hashem, so we should always thank Him and say 'Baruch Hashem'.

date.note: 'This Shabbos is Yud-Tes Kislev'. 19 Kislev fell on Shabbos in 5781 (2020) and 5784 (2023); year not stated.
